question: Born in the U.S.A. tells of a jobless, bitter Vietnam veteran. Why is it so often played as a patriotic anthem?
answer: Because listeners keep the chorus and drop the verses. The title is shouted again and again over a towering drum beat, while the story of a veteran without work or prospects sits in the quieter verses. Campaigning in New Jersey in September 1984, Ronald Reagan praised the message of hope in Springsteen's songs.
move: The line repeated loudest is the one people walk away believing.
ask: When I repeat my main point, is it the one I actually want people to remember?
source: Reagan, remarks in Hammonton, New Jersey, 1984
reference: Reagan, Remarks at a Reagan-Bush Rally in Hammonton, New Jersey, 19 September 1984, Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States
